questions.question: What is a local maximum point of a function $f$?
options: A point where $f$ is at least as large as nearby values of $f$ in the domain
A point where $f$ is larger than every value on the whole domain
questions.explanation: A local maximum point $x_{\mathrm{max}}$ satisfies $f(x_{\mathrm{max}})\ge f(x)$ for all $x$ in some neighbourhood of $x_{\mathrm{max}}$ within the domain.
questions.source_support: The definition uses $f(x_{\mathrm{max}})\ \ge f(x)$ for all nearby $x$ in the domain.
option_explanations: Comparison with the whole domain defines a global maximum, not a local one; a local maximum only needs to beat nearby values.
Undefined points cannot be extrema; $f$ must be defined at $x_{\mathrm{max}}$ for $f(x_{\mathrm{max}})$ to be compared with nearby values.
The value need not be zero; $f(x)=-(x-1)^2+5$ has a local maximum at $x=1$ with value $5\neq 0$.
